title: Imperfect subjunctive: trabajara, comiera
goal: Form and use the imperfect subjunctive in the past and in polite formulas.
theory: The stem comes from the `ellos` form of the indefinido: drop `-ron` and add `-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran`: `trabajaron → trabajara`, `comieron → comiera`, `fueron → fuera`, `tuvieron → tuviera`. There is also a form in `-se`: `trabajase`. It is used where the present subjunctive would be used in the present: after a main verb in the past (`Quería que vinieras`), in unreal conditions (`Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría`) and in a polite request: `Quisiera pedir una mesa.`

title: Perfect subjunctive: haya hecho
goal: Express feelings and doubt about an event that has already happened.
theory: The form is `haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan` + participle: `haya llegado`, `hayas terminado`. It is needed where the subjunctive is required and the action is already completed at the moment of speaking: `Espero que hayas llegado bien.` `Me alegro de que hayáis venido.` `No creo que haya hecho eso.` Compare: `Espero que vengas` (in the future) and `Espero que hayas venido` (it has happened). After `cuando` for a completed future: `Cuando hayas terminado, avísame.`

title: Indicative or subjunctive: certainty and doubt
goal: Choose the indicative or the subjunctive depending on how sure the speaker is.
theory: The indicative is for when the speaker is sure and states a fact, the subjunctive is for doubt, denial and judgement. `Creo que viene` (sure) and `No creo que venga` (doubt). `Es verdad que…` + indicative, `No es verdad que…` + subjunctive. `Pienso que` — indicative, `No pienso que` — subjunctive. If `creer` is in a question, both are possible: `¿Crees que viene?` or `¿Crees que venga?` — the second shows doubt. After `aunque`: a fact takes the indicative, a supposition the subjunctive.

title: Reported speech: dijo que, preguntó si
goal: Report what someone said, asked or requested, matching the tenses.
theory: If the introducing verb is in the present, tenses do not change: `Dice que vive aquí.` If it is in the past, tenses shift: `presente → imperfecto` (`vivo → vivía`), `perfecto → pluscuamperfecto`, `futuro → condicional` (`vendré → vendría`), `imperativo → imperfecto de subjuntivo` (`ven → viniera`). Time words change: `aquí → allí`, `hoy → ese día`, `mañana → al día siguiente`. Questions are introduced by `si` or a question word: `Preguntó si venía.` `Preguntó dónde vivía.`

title: Conditionals with si: real and unreal
goal: Build a real, an unreal and an impossible condition.
theory: There are three types of condition. Real: `si` + present and `present / future / imperative`: `Si llueve, me quedo.` Unreal in the present or future: `si` + imperfect subjunctive and `condicional`: `Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.` Impossible in the past: `si` + pluperfect subjunctive and `condicional perfecto`: `Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.` After `si` in a condition you never put the future or the condicional: `Si tengo tiempo, voy`, not `Si tendré`.

title: Future perfect and conditional perfect
goal: Say that something will be finished by a future moment and guess about the past.
theory: `Futuro perfecto` = `habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán` + participle: `Mañana a las diez habré terminado.` It also expresses a guess about the past: `Habrá llegado ya.` — he has probably arrived. `Condicional perfecto` = `habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habríais, habrían` + participle: `Habría ido, pero estaba enfermo.` It is needed for an impossible condition and for the future in the past: `Dijo que habría terminado.`

title: Concession and result: aunque, a pesar de que, así que
goal: Express concession and result and choose the right mood.
theory: `Aunque` + indicative speaks about a fact: `Aunque llueve, salgo.` (it is raining). `Aunque` + subjunctive is about a supposition or unimportant information: `Aunque llueva, saldré.` (it may rain). `A pesar de que` works the same way, and `a pesar de` goes with a noun and an infinitive. Result: `así que`, `por eso`, `de modo que` + indicative: `Llovía, así que me quedé.` Intensifying: `tan… que`, `tanto… que`: `Estaba tan cansado que se durmió.`

title: Time and purpose: cuando, antes de que, hasta que
goal: Use the subjunctive in clauses of time and purpose when speaking about the future.
theory: If the action has not happened yet, after `cuando`, `hasta que`, `en cuanto`, `después de que`, `mientras` you need the subjunctive: `Cuando llegues, llámame.` If the action is habitual or past, use the indicative: `Cuando llego, siempre te llamo.` After `antes de que` and `para que` the subjunctive is always needed: `Antes de que salgas, cierra la ventana.` If the subject is the same, use `antes de` and `para` with the infinitive: `Antes de salir, cierra.`

title: The passive: ser + participle, passive se
goal: Choose between the passive with ser, the reflexive passive and the impersonal form.
theory: The passive with `ser` = `ser` + a participle that agrees with the subject: `La casa fue construida en 1900.` The agent is introduced by `por`: `fue escrita por Cervantes.` It is typical of written language. In speech the passive `se` is used more often: `Se venden pisos.` `Se habla español.` If the subject is a thing, the verb agrees with it: `se vende una casa`, `se venden casas`. With `estar` + participle you speak about a result: `La puerta está cerrada.`

title: Impersonal sentences with se
goal: Speak in general terms, without naming the doer, using se.
theory: The impersonal `se` + a verb in the third person singular speaks about people in general: `Aquí se trabaja mucho.` `En España se come tarde.` The difference from the passive `se`: after an impersonal verb there is no thing as a subject. With a person as a direct object you need the preposition `a`, and the verb stays singular: `Se busca a los culpables.` Other ways to generalise: `uno`, `la gente`, the `ellos` form: `Dicen que va a llover.`

title: Ser and estar: finer differences
goal: Convey shades of meaning in pairs of ser and estar.
theory: The same adjective with `ser` describes a quality, and with `estar` a state or an impression: `Es guapa` (pretty in general), `Está guapa` (looks nice today). `Es verde` — it is green, `Está verde` — it is unripe. `Es bueno` — good by nature, `Está bueno` — tasty. With `estar` you often speak about a result: `Está terminado`, `Está roto`. To judge an action: `Es difícil` and `Está difícil`. There is no general rule for all words: such pairs are best memorised.

title: The neutral lo: lo bueno, lo que, lo de
goal: Turn an adjective, an adverb or a whole idea into a noun with lo.
theory: `Lo` + adjective gives a general idea: `lo bueno`, `lo importante` — "the good thing", "the important thing". `Lo que` means "what": `Lo que dices es verdad.` `Lo` + adjective + `que` is intensifying: `No sabes lo difícil que es.` `Lo de` introduces a subject: `Lo de ayer fue un error.` — "what happened yesterday". Do not confuse it with the article: `el bueno` (the good one) and `lo bueno` (the good thing). `Lo` can also be a pronoun: `Lo vi.`

title: Work, career and the job interview
goal: Talk about experience, duties and goals at an interview.
theory: At an interview you need verbs of activity and polite formulas: `Me encargo de…`, `Tengo experiencia en…`, `Me gustaría trabajar en…`. Useful words: `el currículum`, `la entrevista`, `el puesto`, `el sueldo`, `el contrato`. To describe skills: `tener capacidad para…`, `trabajar en equipo`.

title: Society and the environment
goal: Discuss general topics: ecology, technology, society.
theory: For discussion you need abstract words and set phrases: `el medio ambiente`, `el cambio climático`, `la contaminación`. Ways to give an opinion: `Es necesario que…`, `Hay que` + infinitive. For an argument: `Por un lado… por otro lado…`. These words are common in news and articles.

title: Linking and introductory words
goal: Build a connected argument using linking words.
theory: For a connected argument you need linking words: adding (`además`, `incluso`), contrast (`sin embargo`, `no obstante`, `en cambio`), reason and result (`por lo tanto`, `por consiguiente`), conclusion (`en conclusión`, `en definitiva`). After some of them a comma is needed: `Sin embargo, no vino.`

title: Reading an opinion article
goal: Understand the author's position, arguments and attitude to the topic.
theory: In an opinion article find the thesis (the main idea), the arguments and the conclusion. Notice evaluative words and linking words: `desde mi punto de vista`, `es evidente que`, `sin embargo`. Tell facts from opinions: facts are in the indicative, opinions and doubts in the subjunctive. After reading, retell the thesis in your own words.

title: Reading an extract from a story
goal: Understand the plot, characters and mood in an extract of fiction.
theory: In a story pay attention to the tenses: indefinido drives the plot, imperfecto creates the background and describes characters. Dialogue in Spanish is marked with dashes: `—¿Dónde vas? —preguntó ella.` After reading answer: who is the hero, what happened, how did it end. Do not be afraid of unknown words: the meaning is clear from context.

title: Writing an argumentative essay
goal: Write a connected text of 150–200 words with a thesis, arguments and a conclusion.
theory: An essay consists of an introduction, two or three arguments and a conclusion. Start with the thesis: `En mi opinión, …`. Then the arguments with linking words: `En primer lugar…`, `Además…`, `Sin embargo…`. Finish with a conclusion: `En conclusión, …`. Use the subjunctive where you express doubt or judgement: `Es necesario que se tomen medidas.`

title: Listening to discussions and debates
goal: Understand the positions of several speakers and each one's arguments.
theory: In a discussion it is important to tell who says what. Listen for formulas of agreement and objection: `Estoy de acuerdo`, `No estoy de acuerdo`, `Eso es cierto, pero…`. Write down each person's points, not separate words. Speakers often interrupt each other and run words together, so listen to the extract two or three times.

title: Listening to a lecture and a talk
goal: Understand the structure of a talk and note down the main ideas.
theory: In a talk catch the structure: the introduction (`Hoy voy a hablar de…`), the points (`en primer lugar`, `en segundo lugar`) and the conclusion (`para terminar`). Write down key words and numbers. If you lose the thread, wait for the next linking word: it will take you back to the structure. Retelling in your own words tests understanding.

vocabulary.translation: Today I am going to talk about…

title: Speaking: debate and argumentation
goal: Defend a position, give an argument and politely object.
theory: The structure of an answer: position, reason, example. `Creo que… porque… Por ejemplo…` For a polite objection: `Entiendo tu punto de vista, pero…`, `No estoy del todo de acuerdo`. Do not raise your voice and do not interrupt: a pause and a clarifying question sound confident. Use the subjunctive for judgements: `Es importante que se escuchen todas las opiniones.`

vocabulary.word: Entiendo tu punto de vista, pero…
vocabulary.translation: I understand your point of view, but…

vocabulary.word: No estoy del todo de acuerdo

vocabulary.translation: What I want to say is…

title: Speaking: a short presentation
goal: Give a 2–3 minute presentation following a plan.
theory: The structure of a presentation: greeting, topic, three points, conclusion. `Buenos días, hoy voy a hablar de… Primero… Después… Por último…` Speak aloud following the plan, do not read. Look at the audience and pause after each point. At the end: `¿Tienen alguna pregunta?`
